messages:
Ashley C: Hey team — high-priority from ACME (support#9876). They report p95 jumping from ~120ms to ~900-1200ms for requests hitting eu-west-1 starting ~11:40 UTC. They attached TTFB traces that show most time in TLS handshake. Can someone pick this up?

Miguel R: on it. first questions: is this all traffic to eu-west or just certain POPs/edges? any config changes/rollouts around 11:30-11:45?

Ashley C: Support says region-wide for them. No product deploys during that window per deploy dashboard. RBAC: no config pushes from infra.

support-bot: Ticket 9876 updated: customer provided cURL timing header outputs, sample: 
```
curl -w "time_namelookup: %{time_namelookup}\ntime_connect: %{time_connect}\ntime_appconnect: %{time_appconnect}\ntime_pretransfer: %{time_pretransfer}\ntime_starttransfer: %{time_starttransfer}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# results: time_namelookup: 0.012\ntime_connect: 0.084\ntime_appconnect: 1.02\ntime_pretransfer: 0.084\ntime_starttransfer: 1.12
```
Basically DNS + TCP is fine, appconnect and starttransfer are large.

Miguel R: that points at TLS handshake (time_appconnect). I can pull edge traces. @oncall drop me the trace ACL.

oncall: ACL sent. Starting tcpdump on eu-west edge pool id=eu-edge-4.

Eva L: I'll check our edge routing autoscaler/route-policy logs. Last control-plane change in eu-west was a minor iptables tweak at 10:50 UTC (bugfix) but nothing at 11:30. Cloud provider reported BGP flaps in eu-west earlier today — filing correlation now.

Miguel R: pulled a 30s pcap around 11:42 from eu-edge-4. TLS Client Hello -> Server Hello gap ~980ms for several flows. Here's the openssl s_time-ish quick check we ran against that host: 
```
openssl s_client -connect edge-01.eu-west.example:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -msg -debug
# observed: full handshake RTTs ~1.0s repeatedly for certain client src subnets
```
Also traceroute from one customer IP to edge shows an extra transit hop: 
```
mtr -rw  -c 10 192.0.2.45
1  gateway  0.5ms
2  transit-a  12ms
3  transit-b  9ms
4  eu-core  450ms  <-- spike here
5  eu-edge-01  10ms
```
looks like one backbone hop intermittently causing retransmits and delaying TLS.

Sam K: I've confirmed multiple customers (not just ACME) complaining from EU region. Support escalated to SEV-2. Notified account execs.

Nina P: any immediate customer-facing mitigations? We can pin region routing to alternative POPs or fallback to our dedicated eu-fallback cluster. But that may cost throughput.

Miguel R: quick mitigations to try in parallel: 
- lower DNS TTL for api.redwood.ai in eu zones to 30s to let clients refresh to healthier edge IPs
- update edge router policy to prefer eu-edge-02/03 (bypass path that hits the flaky backbone) for new sessions (sticky sessions left intact)
- enable TCP zero-window/bulk-retry mitigations (kernel-level) on affected hosts if retransmits high

Eva L: I can flip route preference. pushing a conservative policy change now to route new sessions away from eu-edge-4 via edgectl: 
```
edgectl route set --region eu-west --prefer-pop eu-edge-02,eu-edge-03 --dry-run=false --reason "emergency routing due to backbone spike"
```
Deploy-bot: route-change job queued.

deploy-bot: route-change to prefer eu-edge-02/03 rolled out 11:55:13 UTC to eu-west POPs (canary 20% -> full within 4m).

Miguel R: after the route tweak I see p95 for eu-west customer sample drop to ~140ms within ~2m. p99 still elevated (~600ms) for a small subset. Good sign routing helped.

Ashley C: customer confirms improvement for most requests, says p99 still has occasional 1s spikes. They asked for a root cause and ETA for full resolution.

Eva L: investigating backbone provider logs now. There's a suspected microburst + queueing on one transit link between transit-b and eu-core. We're coordinating with provider to throttle or move traffic. Meanwhile I'll mark eu-edge-4 for deeper network debug and drain if needed.

Miguel R: capturing full TLS handshake PCAP for one of the slow flows — I see multiple retransmits before ServerHello, likely caused by packet loss on that transit hop. Server CPU and app are fine. TLS resumption works fast when client reuses session (so not handshake issue per-se but path loss).

Sam K: sending update to affected customers: "We routed traffic away from the impacted backbone and are working with the transit provider. Most requests should be back to normal; occasional spikes may persist until provider completes mitigations. We'll follow up with a postmortem." :thumbsup:

oncall: placing eu-edge-4 in cordon state and draining connections at 12:08 UTC for hardware/network triage.

deploy-bot: eu-edge-4 cordoned and drain started.

Miguel R: after drain/pinning and provider actions p95 eu-west is back to ~130ms, p99 ~240ms. I'll keep a 15m watch. Creating incident page with links to pcaps/traces.

Eva L: provider confirms packet loss spike between 11:30-12:05 UTC due to transient reroute. They claim BGP route change created a longer path with congestion. They've pushed new adverts and loss cleared at 12:07 UTC.

Ashley C: thanks — please log RCA: root cause = transit backbone reroute + packet loss causing TLS handshake retransmits; mitigations = route pref changes, cordon+drain of affected POP, lowered DNS TTL to expedite client reprobe, provider fix.

Miguel R: adding action items: 
- network: permanent routing policy to avoid that transit peer for high-priority flows (Eva)
- infra: add automated detection for repeated TLS handshake gaps >300ms per-IP and auto-failover to alternate POP (Miguel)
- support: update runbook and customer comms template (Sam)
- SRE: postmortem within 48h, include packet captures and timing graphs (Nina)

Nina P: will own the postmortem. Assigning timeline and stakeholders.

Sam K: customers updated. No billing impact. Marking ticket 9876 as 'monitoring' and will close after 24h of stable metrics.

Ashley C: awesome work. Please link the incident doc when done and leave recommended dashboard alerts (p95/p99 by region + TLS appconnect histogram) for product.

Miguel R: incident doc created: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2025-411 (pcap + graphs attached). Monitoring shows stable since 12:15 UTC. Will follow up on automation next sprint.

deploy-bot: Incident INC-2025-411 created by Miguel R at 12:20 UTC.

support-bot: Ticket 9876 updated: "We routed traffic around the transient backbone issue; monitoring indicates recovery. Please re-open if you see further problems."

Ashley C: closing the escalation here unless anyone sees regressions. If anything pops up tag this thread. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
